t: You're looking at the Old Vic, a nonprofit producing theatre in Waterloo with about a thousand seats. It opened in 1818 as the Royal Coburg Theatre, and was renamed the Royal Victoria Theatre in 1833. Rudolphe Cabanel, a German architect, engineer and machinist known for his work on British theatres, designed it. Emma Cons took it over in 1880, and by then people already called it the Old Vic. Her niece Lilian Baylis took over management in 1898 and began a series of Shakespeare productions in 1914. It has been Grade II star listed since 1951.
